Expected (per API documentation): 400 Bad Request, since "results" must be between 1 and 20.  
Actual: 200 OK and the full product list is returned.  
Note: results=21 and results=-1 are correctly rejected with 400, so only the boundary value 0 is not validated.  
  
Note: for results=-1 the API returns the message "Must be greater than 0", yet results=0 is accepted and returns 200, so the API does not follow its own validation rule.

Expected (per API documentation): 400 Bad Request, since "results" must be an integer between 1 and 20.  
Actual: 200 OK and the full product list is returned.  
Note: the invalid value is ignored instead of being rejected.

Expected (per API documentation): 400 Bad Request, since "results" must be an integer between 1 and 20.  
Actual: 200 OK and the full product list is returned.  
Note: the documentation does not explicitly describe how an empty value should be handled, so the expected result is inferred from the general rule that invalid parameters return 400. The empty value is ignored, same as results=0 and results=abc.

Expected (per API documentation): 400 Bad Request, since "results" must be an integer between 1 and 20.  
Actual: 200 OK and the full product list is returned.  
Note: "null" is sent as a literal text value (query parameters are always strings). It is ignored, same as results=0, results=abc and an empty value.

Expected: 400 Bad Request, since "category" must be one of: coffee, fresh-produce, meat-seafood, candy, dairy, bread-bakery, eggs (the same rule that rejects category=abc).  
Actual: 200 OK and the full product list is returned.  
Note: the empty value is ignored instead of being rejected, same behavior as results= (empty).

Expected: 400 Bad Request, since "available" must be one of: true, false (the same rule that rejects available=abc).  
Actual: 200 OK and the full product list is returned, including out-of-stock items.  
Note: the empty value is ignored instead of being rejected, same behavior as results= and category= (empty).

request.description:
Expected: not defined in the API documentation (only GET /carts/:cartId is described for reading a cart).  
Actual: 404 Not Found with the generic "resource could not be found" message.  
Note: by HTTP convention an unsupported method on an existing route would usually return 405 Method Not Allowed, so this is an observation, not a confirmed defect. The test asserts the current stable behavior.

Expected (business logic): 400 Bad Request, since a quantity of 0 makes no sense for a cart item.  
Actual: 201 Created, the item is added to the cart with quantity 0.  
Note: the API documentation only states that quantity is an optional integer (default 1) and does not define a valid range, so this is not a confirmed documentation violation. It is a suspected business-logic defect, confirmed on two different products (1710 and 2177)

Additional evidence: GET /carts/:cartId shows the item stored with quantity 0. Also, PATCH /carts/:cartId/items/:itemId rejects quantity=0 with 400 ("Invalid or missing quantity."), so the API treats the same value differently depending on the endpoint.EndFragment

Expected (business logic): 400 Bad Request, since a negative quantity makes no sense for a cart item.  
Actual: 201 Created, the item is added to the cart with quantity -1.  
Note: the API documentation only states that quantity is an optional integer (default 1) and does not define a valid range, so this is not a confirmed documentation violation. It is a suspected business-logic defect, confirmed on two different products (2585 and 3486).

Additional evidence: GET /carts/:cartId shows the item stored with quantity -1. Also, PATCH /carts/:cartId/items/:itemId rejects quantity=-1 with 400 ("Invalid or missing quantity."), so the API treats the same value differently depending on the endpoint.
